coverage_note: The input list was already very complete for floating and suspended covers, monolayers, FPV and canal-top PV, pore-diffusion theory, and Portuguese, Spanish, Persian, Turkish, Arabic and Chinese work. Recent 2024-2026 searches on coverage ratio, pan and tank cover experiments, and radiative-cooling covers found no new records. Every relevant hit was already listed, including Duan 2026, Asfahan 2026, Ouchkir 2026, Rezazadeh 2025 and Cardoso 2026. I found four kinds of missing material. (1) Floating-plant covers as natural analogues: the 1970s-1980s water hyacinth, Lemna, Salvinia and Nymphaea evapotranspiration-versus-open-water studies (Brezny 1973, van der Weert 1974, Benton 1978, DeBusk 1983, Anderson 1987, Rao 1988) and recent Lake Tana and NE Brazil macrophyte work. These matter because floating leaves can raise rather than cut water loss, which is a counter-case for S vs phi. (2) Swimming-pool covers, a small-scale literature on covers, energy and evaporation (Francey 1980, Smith 1994, Smedegard 2025). (3) Pan-screen effects (van Dijk 1985, the Australian bird screen on Class A pans). This is directly relevant to suspended-cover sheltering and to bias in pan-based S estimates. (4) Chemical-engineering theory of mass transfer from partially active or heterogeneous surfaces (Flytzani-Stephanopoulos 1979, Stammer 1991, Polyanin 1981). This is a parallel to Schlunder-type gap-diffusion models that the list did not have. Smaller additions: USU/USBR-era grey literature (Hansen 1964 monolayer application, Frasier 1968 alkanol dispersion, Verma wind barriers), the Wichita Falls case study (Verlee), a 2006 Chinese floating-slab design paper, and FPV thermal and wind work (Nysted 2024, Lindholm 2022) for the energy-balance and aerodynamic part. What remains uncovered: the Semantic Scholar query failed (API error), so S2 coverage was not tested. The Russian-language query returned nothing relevant. USBR REC-ERC reports and pre-1970 Indian and Israeli grey literature (e.g. on wax and perlite) are probably not indexed in OpenAlex or Crossref and would need library or catalogue searches. Partial-ice-cover lake flux literature was checked and judged off-target.
